notes: 'was a hundred and twenty years old': the copula and 'old' both belong to the construct בֶּן of the age idiom, the numerals and שָׁנָה keeping their own English (rules 20, 31), the unit discontinuous around the numeral phrase (rule 25).
בְּמֹתוֹ is a noun (מָוֶת) rather than an infinitive, and rule 52's closing sentence still gives 'when' to the temporal preposition, the subject pronoun to the suffix and the predicate to the noun.
'natural force' is headed on 'force'; rule 31's subtraction is close here and the competing head on 'natural' is named in the unit's note.
וְלֹא is fused as 'nor', headed on the negative (rules 23, 35).
